public_rationale: Contemporary evaluations document substantial truthfulness errors, recurring invented information, and repeated narrative inconsistency. This supports the ordinary reading of Marcus's claim. InstructGPT improved substantially, and generation settings affected quality, so the evidence does not support an absolute inability to produce truthful or coherent text.
limitations: The strongest consistency experiment uses synthetic stories.
Generating truthful answers and explicitly classifying truth versus fiction are related but different tasks.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Systems like GPT can't reliably tell truth from fiction; they routinely lose coherence over long passages and fabricate endlessly.

statement.excerpt: One good way to move beyond merely filling in the blanks might be to ask whether the models could reliably distinguish truth from fiction. In point of fact, they can’t. Rather, systems like GPT are truth-challenged, known to routinely lose coherence over long passages of text and known to fabricate endlessly.

from_speaker: routinely lose coherence over long passages of text
our_interpretation: The scope is GPT-3-era models available when the post appeared, including InstructGPT.
The ordinary reading is recurrent factual and narrative failures, not that every answer is false or that fabrication literally never stops.
Long passages means connected, multi-sentence text; Marcus supplies no length threshold.

For this ongoing research assessment, the reporting window is the latest completed calendar year and the current year through publication: 2021-01-01 to 2022-05-21. Research evaluations have no fixed quarterly reporting cycle.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary evaluations show substantial truthfulness failures, repeated fabrication, and recurring inconsistency in connected text.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative contemporary evaluations show dependable factual discrimination and sustained coherence, with fabrication confined to exceptional cases.

evidence.explanation: TruthfulQA tested GPT-3 and other models on 817 questions designed to expose misconceptions. The result supports unreliable truthfulness on this challenge set, not a universal error rate for ordinary use.

evidence.publisher: Nye, Tessler, Tenenbaum and Lake / arXiv
evidence.explanation: All 50 generated stories required at least one sentence to be resampled; the symbolic checker rejected 53.1% of proposed sentences. This demonstrates recurring consistency failures in a controlled narrative domain.

evidence.locator: Section 1, findings on truthfulness and remaining mistakes
evidence.explanation: On closed-domain API tasks, the paper reports invented information in 21% of InstructGPT outputs versus 41% for GPT-3. That supports recurrent fabrication while also showing substantial improvement.

evidence.excerpt: Human text still shows the fewest of these kinds of errors.
evidence.locator: Section 2, key finding 1; qualifications in Section 6.6
evidence.explanation: Scarecrow found fewer factual, commonsense and incoherence errors with larger models. Its best GPT-3 decoding configuration initially matched human annotation counts, although manual review found substantially more genuine errors in GPT-3 text.
